S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in responsibilities at work (e.g., promotion, demotion)
patient_info.stressor: When Terri was asked to take the lead on a larger university convention, her role shifted from behind-the-scenes coordination to greeting vendors, appearing in promotional photos, and speaking briefly at planning meetings. Around that change, she began focusing on a perceived flaw in her face that others barely noticed in candid event photos, and she increasingly organized her day around checking, retaking, or avoiding images before she could move on to planning tasks. The extra time spent managing how she appeared started interfering with vendor calls, meeting preparation, and her usual enjoyment of photography and community events. She eventually sought psychiatric care through a local clinic after a missed planning deadline made her realize the appearance routines were no longer just a private habit.

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: I came in because ever since I’ve had to be more in front of people at work, I can’t stop staring at this one uneven-looking part of my face in photos, even when everyone else says they barely see anything.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: Before I send event pictures or join a vendor meeting, I’ll keep checking my face in my phone camera, retake photos, tilt my head a certain way, or ask a coworker if I look weird, and it can eat up enough time that I fall behind on planning stuff.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I missed part of a planning deadline because I spent so much time dealing with how I looked in the event materials, and now vendor calls and meeting prep take me longer than they should.
